items.title: Branford Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I did a duet once with a young lady named Barbara Krauss. ... Me and Barbara, we played great.

ctx.x: Were you learning repertoire, or were you just learning scales?

I was six, or five, so there’s not much repertoire that a six-year old can learn, unless he’s prodigious, and prodigious I was not, so. I was in a couple of concerts. I did a duet once. I just didn’t like to practice a lot. And I did a duet once with a young lady named Barbara Krauss. I think we were both seven at the time, or eight. My mother was saying, you know, “You’re gonna mess this piece up, because you don’t practice.” So, to lodge a protest, that’s what she said, but I know it’s because of her nerves.…
Now did you have playmates, or other friends who were also involved in music?
